samples.summary: New security comment states the wrong default posture for the only server-side write gate (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`)
samples.evidence: The comment added by this diff says the Yorkie auth webhook is something "a deployment must switch out of its default shadow mode (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`) for a downgrade or a revocation to actually stop a write", and the matching new prose in `docs/design/sharing.md:295-296` says the webhook "is off in a stock deployment". Both are false: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-31` is `raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false'`, i.e. enforcing unless the literal string `false` is set, and `yorkie-auth.controller.ts:121-137` plus `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185` both document enforce-by-default. The same design doc contradicts the new sentence at `docs/design/sharing.md:314` ("**Enforcing is the default**"). An operator or maintainer reading the new text concludes the deployment's only server-side share-link write gate is inert when it is not — and the natural "fix" for such a contradiction is to align the code default to the doc, which would silently disable the gate. No exploit today; the defect is in freshly added security guidance about a control's default posture.

samples.summary: Moving the resolve lookup to POST promotes a high-frequency read into the mutation audit log at `info`
samples.evidence: `customLogLevel` (app.module.ts:51-63) classifies anything that is not GET/HEAD/OPTIONS as a mutation and logs it at `info`, explicitly so that "the audit trail covers doc create, import, share, invite, api-key, datasource". `POST /share-links/resolve` matches neither high-volume path exclusion (`/images`, `/cells`), so every successful re-resolve is now an `info` access-log line. Combined with `SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS = 60_000` plus `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` (shared-document.tsx:1087-1088), that is >=60 info lines per hour per open share tab, where the previous GET form logged at `debug`. The audit-trail signal the comment describes gets diluted by a pure read, and log volume/retention cost rises proportionally to open share tabs. Consider adding `/share-links/resolve` to the `isHighVolumePath` exclusion or keeping the resolve at `debug`.

samples.summary: Revocation staleness is unbounded: any non-404/410 failure preserves the last good `editor` authority indefinitely
samples.evidence: `isShareLinkResolveFatal` returns false whenever `resolved` is set and the error is not a 404/410, and `SharedDocumentByToken` renders `SharedDocumentInner` with the stale `resolved.role` (shared-document.tsx:1103-1119). There is no maximum-staleness cap, so a link revoked or downgraded while the client's re-resolves keep failing — 429 from the shared 120/min-per-IP throttler (app.module.ts:102), a 5xx, an offline laptop, or a client that simply drops the request — keeps presenting `editor` authority for the tab's whole lifetime. `docs/design/sharing.md:302-305` advertises the opposite ("a mounted view gives up its authority within `SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`"). The tradeoff toward availability is deliberate and the Yorkie webhook is the real boundary, but the advertised bound does not hold under the exact failure mode the predicate was written for. A `dataUpdatedAt`-based fallback to `readOnly` after N consecutive failures would make the stated bound true.

samples.summary: `revocableDocStore` forwards raw data properties while live, so a handle dereferenced before `dispose()` is not revoked by it
samples.evidence: In the non-revoked branch the `get` trap does `if (typeof raw !== 'function') return raw;` (read-only.ts:198-199), forwarding the store's own fields — including `YorkieDocStore.doc`, the Yorkie `Document` whose `update()` is the documented write path. `readOnlyDocStore` deliberately hides exactly these (read-only.ts:89-96: "Forwarding those would have left a wider hole than the prototype one below"). The whole premise of `revocableDocStore` (and of `editor.ts:4563-4572`) is that a stale holder captured before the downgrade must go dead at `dispose()`; a holder that captured `getStore().doc` rather than the wrapper keeps a fully writable CRDT handle, because revocation only intercepts future property reads. No in-repo caller does this today (`docs-find-bar` keeps the wrapper object), so I could not complete an exploit chain — hence medium confidence. Hiding non-function properties in both states would close it without changing any live behaviour the editor relies on.
searchedFor: grep getStore() usages in packages/frontend and packages/docs

samples.summary: The token-in-path `GET /share-links/:token/resolve` is retained indefinitely with no deprecation, removal condition, or test pinning its eventual removal
samples.evidence: The entire stated rationale for the new POST form (controller.ts:68-82, `api/share-links.ts:99-105`) is that a share token in a path segment is written into "every access log, proxy and CDN between the visitor and this handler". The GET route stays public and unguarded, justified as "for the one-shot callers that already exist (an older frontend served during a rollout)" — but a repo-wide grep finds no remaining caller (only tests, `log-safe-url.spec.ts`, and docs), and nothing records when it may be removed. The leak class the change exists to close therefore remains permanently reachable. Related and worth noting in the same breath: the frontend route itself is `/shared/<token>`, so the credential is still in the browser URL, history, and any outbound `Referer` (no `Referrer-Policy` found in packages/frontend), meaning "the token stays out of URLs" holds only for this one API call.

samples.summary: `refetchOnWindowFocus` + `staleTime: 0` on an unauthenticated endpoint sharing one 120/min per-IP throttle bucket can self-inflict 429s on unrelated routes
samples.evidence: The query sets `refetchInterval: 60_000`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` and `staleTime: 0` (shared-document.tsx:1087-1089), so every tab focus issues a fresh `POST /share-links/resolve`. `ThrottlerModule.forRoot` uses a single bucket of 120 requests/60s shared across *all* routes and keyed per IP (app.module.ts:97-104), and the share-link controller carries no `@SkipThrottle`. Rapid tab switching, or several visitors behind one NAT/corporate egress IP, burns that shared budget on a read that changes almost never, and the resulting 429s hit unrelated API calls (document saves, image uploads) for the same IP. It also feeds finding #3: a 429 is classified non-fatal, so the throttled client keeps its stale authority. A dedicated looser/`@SkipThrottle` treatment plus a non-zero `staleTime` would decouple the two.

samples.summary: Public endpoint's only input validation is a hand-rolled `typeof` check that sits outside the global ValidationPipe
samples.evidence: `resolveByBody` declares `@Body() body: { token?: unknown }` — an inline TS type with no metatype class — so the global `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })` in `main.ts:65-72` performs no validation or stripping here. The single line `typeof body?.token === 'string' ? body.token : ''` is what keeps a non-scalar (e.g. `{"token":{"not":""}}`) from reaching `prisma.shareLink.findUnique({ where: { token } })` in `share-link.service.ts:103`. It is correct today, and Prisma's `findUnique` would likely reject a filter object anyway, so this is not exploitable — but the repo's convention everywhere else is a validated DTO, and an unauthenticated endpoint whose only guard is one inline conditional is the wrong place to diverge from it. A `ResolveShareLinkDto` with `@IsString() @IsNotEmpty()` would make the guard structural rather than incidental.
searchedFor: glob packages/backend/src/share-link/* for a dto file

finding.summary: The new 60-second revalidation loop repeatedly puts the access-granting share token in a request URL, amplifying an exposure the repo deliberately avoids elsewhere
finding.evidence: `resolveShareLink` sends the capability token in the URL path of an unauthenticated GET: `${API}/share-links/${seg(token)}/resolve` (share-links.ts:103). Before this change that happened once per page load. `SharedDocumentByToken` now sets `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` (60_000) plus `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` (shared-document.tsx:1125-1126), so every open tab writes the token into reverse-proxy/CDN/nginx access logs, APM traces and devtools network history ~60x/hour for as long as the tab lives. The repo already treats this exact token as too sensitive for a URL: `fetchYorkieShareToken` comments "POST with the token in the body (not the URL) so this access-granting token stays out of request URLs and server access logs" (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:190-197) and POSTs it instead. Anyone with read access to those logs replays the token at `/shared/:token` and gets the document with whatever role the link carries — including `editor`. The backend route is `@Get('share-links/:token/resolve')` (packages/backend/src/share-link/share-link.controller.ts:67), so the fix is a POST-body sibling route, matching the yorkie-token endpoint.

verdict.reason: The claimed evidence does not exist. `resolveShareLink` (packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:107-124) POSTs to `/share-links/resolve` with `body: JSON.stringify({ token })` — the token is in the request body, never in the URL path; there is no `${API}/share-links/${seg(token)}/resolve` anywhere in the frontend (grep for `resolveShareLink` and `/resolve\`` returns only share-links.ts:111 and the single caller shared-document.tsx:1085). Therefore the 60 s `refetchInterval`/`refetchOnWindowFocus` loop (shared-document.tsx:1087-1088) writes nothing sensitive into access logs; it repeats a POST body. The fix the finding recommends ("a POST-body sibling route, matching the yorkie-token endpoint") is already implemented server-side at packages/backend/src/share-link/share-link.controller.ts:84-89 (`@Post('share-links/resolve')`), and the retained legacy `@Get('share-links/:token/resolve')` (line 91) is covered by the token-redaction rule `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS` in packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts:87-113, which normalizes case/percent-encoding/duplicate slashes before masking. No exposure chain exists as described.
